title: Carrier Trace Terms for Delivery Claims, by Claim Type
content:
Carrier Relations terms for Delivery Claims: which claim types run a carrier trace before decision, how long the trace runs, when a Lost in Transit parcel counts as lost, and how quickly a claim is decided once it reaches review.

| Claim type | Carrier trace before decision | Trace period (business days) | Parcel treated as lost | A trace answer of delivered confirmed leads to denial | Decision within (business days of reaching under review) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Late Delivery Claim | not required | 0 (no trace) | not applicable | no | 2 |
| Delivered Not Received Claim | required | 5 | not applicable | no | 2 |
| Lost in Transit Claim | required | 8 | on the carrier's lost confirmation, or when the trace period ends without an answer | yes, unless the claim is converted to a non-receipt claim | 1 |
| Damaged in Transit Claim | not required | 0 (no trace) | not applicable | no | 2 |
| Missing Item Claim | not required | 0 (no trace) | not applicable | no | 2 |
| Wrong Item Claim | not required | 0 (no trace) | not applicable | no | 2 |

## Notes on the terms

- A trace runs for its period in business days; a trace on a Delivered Not Received Claim runs 5 business days and one on a Lost in Transit Claim runs 8 business days. When the period ends without a carrier answer, the trace concludes without a response.
- A Lost in Transit parcel counts as lost on either of two grounds: the carrier confirms it lost, or the trace period elapses. Both grounds are sufficient on their own.
- A carrier answer that the parcel was delivered denies a Lost in Transit Claim unless the claim is converted to a non-receipt claim; for every other type this term does not apply.
- Decision time is counted in business days from the day the claim reaches under review: 1 business day for a Lost in Transit Claim, 2 business days for every other type.
